topic: Ohio E-Check can fail you on readiness monitors even with the check-engine light off
mechanicTruth: Ohio's E-Check emissions test (required in Cuyahoga County and six neighboring NE Ohio counties) can reject a vehicle for too many incomplete OBD-II readiness monitors, independent of whether the check-engine light (MIL) is illuminated. Readiness monitors reset to 'Not Ready' after a battery disconnect, a cleared trouble code, or an ECU replacement, and require completed drive cycles to re-set before the vehicle can pass.
driverConfusion: Drivers assume 'the light's off, I'm fine' and are surprised by an E-Check rejection that has nothing to do with a broken part — it's an incomplete self-check, not a fault.
clevelandAngle: E-Check is a Cuyahoga County (plus six neighboring NE Ohio counties) requirement tied directly to vehicle registration — failing it blocks your plates, not just your dashboard.

selectedCaption: Light's off on your dash. You still failed E-Check. Here's the part nobody explains: Ohio's E-Check doesn't just read your check-engine light — it reads whether your car's own readiness monitors finished re-checking themselves after a battery disconnect or a cleared code. No light doesn't mean ready. Drive it a bit, let the monitors finish, then test. Cuyahoga E-Check questions? Stop by and we'll take a look. #ECheck
